transcript: Okay, I mostly agree with this video, so I'm gonna piggyback on one part of it and push back a little bit on another part. Essentially, this creator is talking about how musicals like ragtime or Gypsy are so good and so beloved that they actually are at a disadvantage in the revival category at the Tonys because the voters tend to favor more reimagined productions, and these musicals don't really warrant reimagining. I absolutely think there's truth to that, which is, like, kind of a shame, I guess, because I do think that, you know, at least half of what it takes to put on a good revival is choice of material and, you know, timing of the material. To be clear, though, that isn't to say that I think ragtime should win best revival. I'm actually very much team cats, because the reimagining is just so abnormally brilliant that it kind of supersedes all that other stuff about timing and choice of material. But in general, broadly speaking, I think those factors should be considered more than they have been recently. Especially because the Tony doesn't even go to the director who reimagined it. It goes to the producers who decided to put it on. But while I do think the phenomenon this creator is describing is very real, on the other side, I can't help but think about, like, the recent Hello, Dolly revival, which was as traditional of production as you could possibly imagine, but it Did win Best Revival at the Tonys simply because it was just so ridiculously good, where it was so tightly locked in on what made this material good, what made it work, that it was kind of able to blossom into the fullest potential of what the material had to offer. It was talent and understanding, but also kind of an X factor. And I would argue that it's that X factor and that sense of being really locked in has maybe been missing from some of these recent traditional revivals. And obviously that's subjective. There are a lot of people, including you, possibly, who feel that the ragtime revival does have that X factor, but I think also a lot of people who don't, especially when it comes to the staging and what have you. And we can all agree to disagree on that, case by case. But I would still argue that that middle ground does exist between the reimagined production and the one that just takes the material, puts it on a platter, says, there it is, isn't it good? And calls it a day.
classificationReason: Creator discusses Tony Awards revival category dynamics, references Ragtime, Gypsy, and CATS. Expresses opinion on CATS's reimagining being 'abnormally brilliant' but this is awards commentary, not a first-hand review of the production.
